title: Cargo Liability, CargoCare and Cargo Claims: Notice Periods After Delivery for Each Tier
content:
For each tier of `Cargo Liability, CargoCare and Cargo Claims`, three periods fix how long after delivery written notice of a loss may reach the line. All three are counted in calendar days from the delivery of the cargo.

## The periods

- **Hidden loss period.** The calendar days after delivery within which notice of a loss that was not apparent when the cargo was delivered must reach the line.
- **Visible loss period.** The calendar days after delivery within which notice of a loss that was apparent at delivery must reach the line. A figure of 0 means that such a loss has to be noted on the delivery receipt itself.
- **Delay loss period.** The calendar days after delivery within which notice of a delay loss must reach the line.

## Quick reference (calendar days after delivery)

| Tier | Hidden loss | Visible loss | Delay loss |
|---|---|---|---|
| `AHL Standard Carrier Liability` | 3 | 0 | 0 |
| `AHL Declared Value Liability` | 3 | 0 | 0 |
| `AHL CargoCare Essential` | 7 | 0 | 0 |
| `AHL CargoCare Plus` | 14 | 3 | 0 |
| `AHL CargoCare Premium` | 21 | 3 | 0 |
| `AHL CargoCare Total` | 30 | 7 | 21 |

## Reading the table

- A figure of 0 in the visible loss column, which appears for the three lowest tiers, signals the delivery receipt notation rather than a count of days.
- Only `AHL CargoCare Total` shows a delay loss period above zero, at 21 days.
- The hidden loss period lengthens as the tiers rise, from 3 days at the statutory tier to 30 days at the top tier.
